title: tenant-ledger-cost-pruner-and-auto-quant-scout
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Introduce tenant ledger based cost-pruner and an auto-quant-scout service that suggests per-tenant quantization tiers and cache TTLs. No breaking API changes; feature gated behind runtime config and tenant flags.
description:
Context and motivation: High-variance tenant workloads were producing suboptimal unit economics due to one-size-fits-all batching and cache TTL defaults. This PR introduces a lightweight tenant ledger cost-pruner that synthesizes historical serving ledgers to identify low-value token paths (high cost, low utility) and applies conservative runtime hints (cache TTL adjustments and batching preference) plus an Auto-Quant Scout that recommends per-tenant quant profiles for offline review.

Design summary: The change is composed of two coordinated parts: (1) ledger-cost-pruner: an offline+online component that processes tenant serving ledgers (sampled summaries) and emits ranked pruning suggestions (e.g. reduce KV cache TTL for chat-conversations with >70% repeated prefixes, down-prioritize medium-length generative paths for spot tenants), and (2) quant-scout: a shrink-wrapped service that runs cheap calibration runs on representative request samples and scores quantization candidates (FP16, W4x8, W8A8) on quality delta + cost delta. The runtime consumes service hints via a new lightweight config endpoint and exposes a BestEffort apply path behind tenant opt-in.

What changed (high level):
- runtime/ledger/pruner: new pruning policy engine + tenant sampling adapter (go).
- optimizer/quant/scout: auto-scorer and offline candidate evaluator (python) with CLI to export suggestions as CSV/JSON.
- console: UI stub to surface scout recommendations under Tenant -> Cost Insights.
- infra: new k8s Job manifest that runs scout calibrations asynchronously for tenants flagged for scouting.
- docs: operation guide and safety checklist.

Testing and validation:
- unit tests for pruning heuristics and quant-scout scoring (added ~30 tests).
- integration test simulating 10k requests across 50 synthetic tenants to verify no latency regression and conservative application of hints.
- bench: microbench of runtime hint apply path shows median p95 latency increase <1ms, token cost reduction simulated at ~7% on the synthetic workload.

Rollout plan: feature-gated (runtime flag = ledger_pruner_enabled); staged rollout: internal alpha tenants -> beta tenants via console opt-in -> gradual auto-suggest rollout after 2-week monitoring window. Safe-fallbacks: any applied pruning is reversible and annotated in tenant audit logs; quant-scout recommendations require explicit operator review before enforced quantization on Dedicated/Private clusters.

Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-1942) [x] unit/integration tests [x] e2e bench run [x] UI stub [x] infra manifests [x] telemetry hooks added

Related work: complements cost-probe and tenant-warmstart tooling, but differs by leveraging ledger-derived marginal cost signals and producing per-tenant quant recommendations for human review.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps auto-apply conservative: runtime will only apply cache TTL and batching hints initially; quant application is manual until we have longer-term quality telemetry.
